title: A day of comments as one row, and a bell for the file that won’t stop
summary: Three or more comments on a file in one day now arrive as a single row that opens into the day itself. Choose whether only mentions become tasks, and silence one noisy file without losing the project it lives in.
added: Choose whether only comments that name you become tasks, or every comment does. The switch is in Settings › Apps › Figma.
Mute a single file inside a watched project or team. Expanding one lists the files under it with what each has said lately, and a bell silences the noisy one.
A busy day arrives as one row. One or two comments still appear as ordinary rows; three or more collapse into “Agenda v4 — 10 comments, 3 mention you”.
Open that row and you get the day itself — the comments naming you first, the rest under them. Tap one to open it on its own, with its thread and a place to reply.
A Figma row closes itself once every comment that named you that day is resolved in Figma. It is logged as closed by the app, so it never reads as something you finished.
After you send a reply, the composer offers “Mark done” for one tap. Replying is not finishing, so it is offered and never assumed.
improved: The design sits in a panel of its own height with Figma’s pin on it, so a comment on a long screenshot no longer pushes the conversation off the screen, and you can see which part it is about. Tap it for full size.
The design is kept after the first look and fetched ahead of you during a sync, so it is usually on screen the moment you open a comment rather than a few seconds later.
Your day is your day. A task stays on the day it arrived until you tick it, and each day on the strip carries its own count.
The menu, ⋯ and Back buttons are smaller, and the same size as each other.
fixed: Scrolling, properly this time — a row’s own swipe now steps aside for a vertical drag, so the list moves wherever on it you start.
The same Figma comments could show twice — once as separate rows and once as the day’s collection.

title: Figma comments that actually arrive, and answering them without leaving
summary: Figma mentions reach the agenda as tasks you can answer without leaving the app — the reply posts into the same thread, and the design the comment points at sits above it.
added: Reply to a Figma comment from inside the app. The reader has a composer that posts into the same thread, and what you sent stays on screen.
The design the comment points at is shown above it, the way Figma’s own comment view does — “change this text” means little without the screen it is about.
Three suggested replies under every Figma comment, written for design feedback: on it, when, or which part exactly. They appear when you tap the field.
Settings › Apps › Figma now has a Watched files list. Paste any Figma link and the app reads comments from it; a project or team link covers everything inside, including files added later.
Copied a Figma link already? The list offers it as one tap instead of asking you to paste.
Figma links written in Slack messages and email are picked up on their own and listed as found in a message.
Three greetings a day — 10:30, 13:00 and 18:00 — each with a short line written for that hour, rotating through the week.
improved: Tapping a Figma comment opens the reader instead of jumping straight to Figma. Open in Figma is still the first button there.
The header stays put — title, greeting and the date strip — and only the list moves under it.
A task is filed by what its own summary concluded, so a row can no longer say “needs your reply” while the card inside it says the opposite.
Each watched Figma file is read at its own pace — often while a conversation is live, rarely once it has gone quiet.
A Figma file’s name is shown on the row, so a mention says where it happened.
When Figma refuses a token it now says what is actually missing, rather than just “refused”.
fixed: Figma comments could never start arriving. The app only read files it had learned about from Figma’s notification email, and the whole point of reading comments is that the email does not always come.
The app crashed on opening for anyone with Figma connected.
The list would refuse to scroll depending on which row you started the drag on.
A pasted team link larger than twenty files never read past the first twenty.
Replies could be sent to the wrong place in a comment thread.

title: Apps hub, meeting prep, custom instructions, and a much faster sync
summary: Meeting prep briefs, an Apps hub with Figma and Notion, free-form custom instructions, a No action needed section, and a sync that is noticeably faster.
added: Apps hub in the menu: Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Figma and Notion in one place, with multiple Figma and Notion accounts via pasted tokens.
Figma and Notion mentions, comments, shares and invites arrive as tasks; tapping one opens the file or page in its app.
Figma mentions are also read straight from Figma’s comments, so they arrive even when Figma’s notification email is off or delayed.
Custom instructions per app: free-form text — skip, ignore, prioritise or deprioritise whatever you describe.
Reply tone: System, or your own voice learned from messages you’ve sent.
Meeting prep on every meeting: who’s coming, what you discussed with them on Slack, what’s likely to come up, and who to confirm with. A recurring meeting is briefed since you last met.
A “No action needed” section for updates you might want to read but don’t owe a reply to.
Notifications for new tasks, and a daily brief at 10:30.
Swipe right on any task to complete it; haptic feedback throughout the app.
Settings › Activity Log now shows what each sync read, created and hid.
New app icon.
improved: Fetching is noticeably faster: the Slack and Gmail openers run at once instead of queueing, and the AI no longer spends time thinking before structured answers.
The sync covers the whole day from midnight, and Slack thread replies are included, not just top-level messages.
Open tasks carry over to today until you finish them; a completed task sits on the day you finished it.
Tomorrow’s meetings appear on the date strip and are briefed the evening before.
A meeting that isn’t today, or runs past midnight, shows its day in the time.
fixed: Tasks skipped by your custom instructions were deleted permanently. They are now hidden instead, the agenda says how many, and changing the instruction brings them back.
You could get a “new tasks” notification with nothing new on today’s list — tasks from earlier days were filed under the day their message was sent.
Slack user IDs showing in place of names.
A rescheduled meeting still showed its old time.
